stories.label: Two scenarios for the Yemen war
stories.summary: A week of Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport and Aramco sites has ended Saudi Arabia's bet that it could 'contain' Yemen's war while pouring money into growth at home. The development: analysts and diplomats now call the containment strategy collapsed, the gravest test of Mohammed bin Salman's rule. Lead with what the strikes have cost the kingdom (flights, oil sites, the tourism pitch) and lay out the two paths, escalation with or without US help or a deal with Sanaa, and who in Yemen pays for each. Brent crude is the series moving with it.

stories.label: Kenya's health ministry confirms second Ebola case
stories.summary: Kenya has a second confirmed Ebola case, a 39-year-old contact who fell ill in quarantine ten days after the first case, which travelled from Congo through Uganda (first death covered 2026-10-06). The development is the second case. That it surfaced inside quarantine means contact tracing caught it. Lead with that, then the cross-border chain from Congo's outbreak, now past 9,000 cases, and what Kenya and Uganda are doing at the border.

stories.label: Pulling Out Teeth Just to Live: How Israel Has Devastated Dental Care in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has barred dental materials from Gaza for three years along with other medical supplies, so patients choose between treatment they can't afford, having teeth pulled, or living on painkillers. Lead with the extraction: a treatable infection ends in a lost tooth because fillings and anaesthetic are blocked. The mechanism is how the siege's restricted-items rules reach ordinary care, and who decides what counts as restricted. Use the dentists' own figures.

stories.label: Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing
stories.summary: Officials told Mada Masr that Egypt and Sudan are negotiating a joint security framework for their eastern border after the airstrike on a Halayeb Triangle gold mine that killed scores of Sudanese miners (72 dead, covered 2026-10-11). The development is the framework, sold as action against 'organised crime'. Lead with who the miners were and who struck them, then ask whose security the deal serves in a disputed triangle Egypt administers and Sudan claims. Public anger in Sudan is the pressure behind it.

stories.label: Pakistani, Chinese armies begin joint training exercise in Xinjiang
stories.summary: Pakistan's army opened 'Karakoram 2026', a counterterrorism exercise with China's PLA at Korla in Xinjiang. Lead with the setting: Pakistani troops training under a counterterrorism banner in the province where China holds Uyghurs in mass detention. The mechanism is what Islamabad gets from the alliance (security on the CPEC corridor, arms) and what it costs Pakistan to say nothing about Xinjiang. China's military account announced the exercise, so attribute the details.

stories.label: SWS: Sept involuntary hunger surges to 22.6%
stories.summary: The Social Weather Stations survey found 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry in September, a sharp rise. Lead with the figure and the number of households it means. The mechanism is the war-driven fuel and food prices reaching an import-dependent economy, and what Manila is doing about it. NOTE: the Inquirer piece is the story. The Al Jazeera source in this cluster is a mismatch about US inflation; do not use it.

stories.label: AT&T is selling its Mexican business for $2 billion
stories.summary: AT&T is leaving Mexico, selling AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash plus contingent payments. Lead with the exit: a US carrier that spent more than a decade building Mexico's challenger network to Carlos Slim's América Móvil is handing it to a domestic media giant. The mechanism is what consolidation means for Mexican mobile prices and competition, and whether regulators can block it. Dateline Mexico City.

stories.label: Trump administration delays new rule that could restrict imported medicines from Canada and overseas
stories.summary: The administration has pushed back by 90 days a rule, due on Oct. 22, that would have cut off Americans who buy prescription drugs from licensed pharmacies in Canada and overseas. Lead with the decision and who relies on those imports: patients priced out of US drug costs. The mechanism is the de minimis change that would have blocked the parcels, and the pharmaceutical lobby that benefits from closing the channel.

stories.label: Triplet of ‘Ghostly’ Galaxies Hints at What Dark Matter Is — and Isn’t
stories.summary: Three galaxies that seem to have almost no dark matter look like the debris of a single collision, which pulled ordinary matter away from dark matter. Lead with why that matters: if a collision can separate them, dark matter is a real substance, and theories that explain it away by modifying gravity can't account for these galaxies. Explain the mechanism in plain terms and name the observers and the instrument.

stories.label: 'World's oldest known' shipwreck revealed with Sydney archaeologist's help
stories.summary: Archaeologists say a wreck in the shallows off Kekova Island in Turkey dates to about 4,500 years ago, the age of the Great Pyramid, which would make it the oldest known shipwreck. Lead with the date and how the cargo's ceramics fixed it. What it shows is Bronze Age seaborne trade across the eastern Mediterranean, Egypt included, earlier than the record has shown. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: NASA's embattled Venus missions are back on track after cancellation threat
stories.summary: NASA's DAVINCI and VERITAS missions, which had been threatened with cancellation, are back on course to launch for Venus in the early 2030s. Lead with the decision and the science: DAVINCI will drop a probe through the atmosphere to settle whether Venus once had oceans. The mechanism is the budget fight that nearly killed them, and how much of the first return to Venus in a generation rests on ESA's EnVision.

stories.label: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the throttling: Musk now says the US government was behind the slowdown of Ukraine's military-grade Starshield service, which hampered drone strikes and air defence overnight. Lead with the claim, and with what it means if Washington can switch off an ally's battlefield links through a contractor and deny it. Explain how Starshield differs from consumer Starlink and who controls access to it.

stories.label: Norway’s Telenor telecom faces lawsuit for giving user data to Myanmar junta
stories.summary: Telenor, majority-owned by the Norwegian state, is being sued for handing Myanmar subscribers' data to the military junta and for a divestment that left the network, with its call records and location data, to a junta-linked buyer. Lead with the people harmed: activists tracked and arrested. The mechanism is how a European telco's compliance with 'lawful intercept' orders and its exit became surveillance tools. It sets a precedent for corporate liability.

stories.label: Mexico to force Meta, TikTok, and X to better protect minors on platform
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum signed a decree requiring TikTok, Meta and X to restrict, by design, minors' exposure to violent, sexual and other harmful content. Lead with the 'by design' duty, which puts the obligation on how the platforms are built, not on moderation after the fact. The mechanism is what enforcement and penalties the decree carries, and whether Mexico, a market of tens of millions of young users, can make US platforms comply where the US has not. Dateline Mexico City.

stories.label: 智能体长任务总“失忆”？国产开源破局，类Jev模型接管Agent调度
stories.summary: Beijing's APUS has open-sourced Reflex Agent under the MIT licence. It hands an agent's control decisions (what to do next, whether a task is done) to a 4.5B-parameter decision model fine-tuned from Qwen3.5 instead of calling a large model at every step, and claims 2-3x faster responses. Lead with that design choice, then the 'lossless memory' scheme, which retrieves raw history instead of compressed summaries for long tasks. A Chinese lab's answer to the latency and forgetting problems every agent builder has. Treat the speed figures as the company's own claims.

stories.label: Container carrier sinks in Strait of Hormuz after explosion
stories.summary: New development on the arc where six ships were hit on 10-13: the IRGC Navy says a ship carrying more than 2,500 containers sank after striking a naval mine while using an 'unauthorized' route. Lead with the sinking and the mine: Iran is now claiming a route-permission regime over an international strait, and a mined lane changes the risk for every crew and insurer, not just Iran-linked tankers. Attribute the IRGC's account to Iranian state media; note CENTCOM's role where sources give it. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Zelensky: I feel betrayed by Trump
stories.summary: In London, Zelensky said he feels betrayed by Trump and that Russia showed 'ostentatious disrespect' by defying the energy truce Kyiv honoured by pausing refinery strikes. Lead with that asymmetry: Ukraine gave up its main economic weapon and Moscow kept striking. Britain vowed faster anti-drone missile deliveries, and Ukraine claims 101 sq km retaken near Lyman. The structural point: a truce brokered by Washington with no enforcement binds only the side that depends on Washington.

stories.label: Trump Appeals Order Restoring CNN, MS NOW White House Access
stories.summary: The Justice Department appealed a federal judge's order that keeps CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists inside the White House while they sue over Trump's ban. Lead with the appeal and the First Amendment question: can a president choose which outlets cover him? The mechanism: access as a lever — outlets that lose the briefing room lose the questions. Same week as Turkey seizing Halk TV and Pakistan's live-coverage ban; keep it to the US case.

stories.label: Pemra directs TV channels to refrain from broadcast, live coverage of 'unpleasant incidents', including terror attacks
stories.summary: Pakistan's media regulator ordered every satellite channel to stop broadcasting, rebroadcasting or covering live any 'explosion, blast, firing, terrorist attack etc.' Lead with the breadth of the order: 'firing' covers police live fire, which comes days after police opened fire on PTI protesters in Bara. The mechanism: a blanket safety rule that lets the state decide which violence the public sees. Note what penalties the order threatens.

stories.label: Protests at several prisons, detainee ‘banishments’ surround delay to Criminal Procedure Code
stories.summary: Detainees held beyond Egypt's legal limits on pretrial detention protested in several prisons after the new Criminal Procedure Code's start was delayed, and lawyers describe 'banishments' — transfers to distant facilities — as the response. Lead with the prisoners held past the legal maximum: the delay keeps them jailed with no charge resolved. The mechanism: 'recycling' and remand renewals that a new code was supposed to cap. Rights groups want an independent review.

stories.label: ASML's chip equipment sales to China soar 109% despite US export curb push
stories.summary: ASML's results explain a share price down 7.7% in a week: shipments to China more than doubled (109%) and China will be about 20% of sales this year, even as Washington pushes the Netherlands to tighten export rules, while the company forecast fourth-quarter sales above expectations on AI chip demand. Lead with the China number. The mechanism: the Dutch firm's growth depends on the market US policy wants to close, so its stock trades on Washington's next rule, not its order book.

stories.label: Brazil rare earth deal proves militaries’ long-held interest in minerals
stories.summary: The US Department of War has invested in Brazil's Serra Verde rare-earth mine, the only large ionic-clay producer outside China. Lead with who now finances the mine and what share of output goes where. The mechanism: 'critical minerals' began as a military stockpiling term, and Washington is again buying supply security in the Global South with defence money. Who in Goiás bears the mine's costs, and what Brasília gets in return.

stories.label: CBN restates single-digit inflation target as FG woos investors with tax credits
stories.summary: Nigeria's central bank governor committed to single-digit inflation, calling inflation 'the biggest threat to the poor', as the federal government offers investors tax credits. Lead with the gap between the target and current inflation, and what the target commits the CBN to on rates. The mechanism: a tight-money promise paired with fiscal giveaways to investors — who pays if the two pull against each other. Name the series: the naira.

stories.label: Germany urges Russia to halt Black Sea attacks threatening grain supplies
stories.summary: Germany's foreign minister Wadephul asked Russia to agree a ceasefire for civilian shipping in the Black Sea, warning that continued strikes on vessels risk hunger in Africa — after drones sank a ship off Bulgaria. Lead with what is at stake for grain importers in Africa and the Middle East, not the statement itself: which corridor, which volumes, which buyers. The mechanism: war-risk insurance and attacks on ships near NATO waters raise the delivered price of wheat. Name the series: wheat.

stories.label: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
stories.summary: Researchers used AI to design proteases from scratch — enzymes that cut peptide bonds that otherwise last hundreds of years. Lead with what the designed enzymes cut and how well against natural ones. The mechanism: moving protein design from binding (holding a target) to catalysis (breaking it), which opens targeted destruction of disease proteins. Name the lab, the journal, and the limits.

stories.label: We can rescue the AMOC after its collapse - but it won't be easy | New Scientist
stories.summary: A modelling study (Danish Meteorological Institute) finds a climate-driven collapse of the Atlantic overturning circulation might be reversible — but only with large cuts in warming over a long time. Lead with what it would take to restart it and how long. Who bears a collapse: monsoon failures in West Africa and South Asia, not only cold European winters. Report the uncertainty plainly.

stories.label: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
stories.summary: A Nature Communications study finds fever-range temperatures make host cells better at killing bacteria while protecting their mitochondria from damage. Lead with the measured effect. The mechanism and the practical question it raises: routine fever suppression with antipyretics may blunt a defence the body evolved, at a time when antibiotic resistance is rising. State whether this is cells, animals or patients.

stories.label: Europäischer Datenschutzausschuss: Smartbrillen sind „hohes Risiko für Grundrechte und Freiheiten“
stories.summary: The European Data Protection Board published its first guidelines on camera smart glasses such as Meta's, calling them a 'high risk to fundamental rights and freedoms' and demanding clearer signals when they film or record. Lead with that classification and what it obliges makers and wearers to do. The mechanism: glasses that look ordinary turn every bystander into a data subject who never consented. Alibaba launched its own Qwen camera glasses in China the same day — one line of context, no more.

stories.label: Urteil zu Betrugswerbung: „Es ist nicht mehr diese plumpe Masche von früher“
stories.summary: A Frankfurt regional court ruled in Finanzfluss v. Meta that Meta is responsible for fraudulent investment ads run on Instagram and Facebook using the founder's likeness. Lead with the ruling: a platform held liable for scam ads it was paid to run. The precedent: ad revenue from fraud stops being someone else's problem, which could reach every victim of deepfake celebrity-investment scams in Europe. Note whether Meta appeals.

stories.label: Microsoft to restrict AI-generated images of candidates ahead of 2027 election -- Official
stories.summary: Microsoft will load INEC's final candidate list into its generative-AI tools to block fabricated images of Nigerian candidates before the 2027 election. Lead with the mechanism: a name list as a guardrail — which covers Microsoft's tools only, not open models or rival platforms where deepfakes circulate. Who decides what counts as 'unrealistic', and whether Nigeria gets the same protection US and EU elections do.

stories.label: U.S. inflation rises to 3.7% in September report - AOL
stories.summary: US inflation rose 0.6% in September to 3.7% a year, up from 3.4%, with gasoline up 9.1% in the month — the war-driven oil shock reaching American pumps in the last data release before the midterms. The consequences landed at once: traders added bets on Fed rate hikes, the dollar index hit its highest since May 2025, bitcoin fell sharply, and the same figure set a 3.6% cost-of-living rise for 71 million Social Security beneficiaries. Name the series: US inflation, the Fed rate, the US 10-year Treasury yield, bitcoin, Brent crude.

stories.label: Mercuria Agrees $250 Million Congo Copper Deal With China Miner
stories.summary: Swiss trader Mercuria is prepaying $250 million for Congolese copper from units of China's Shanghai Jayson — a European trading house financing a Chinese miner to secure an African metal, with Congo itself absent from the deal. Lead with the prepayment mechanism: trading houses now act as banks to lock up supply, while Reuters reports the US copper stockpile built on Trump's tariff threat is unwinding. Name the series: copper.

stories.label: High on wins in Tigray, Ethiopia now has Eritrea in its crosshairs
stories.summary: Ethiopia invoked Article 51 self-defence at the UN Security Council, saying Eritrean troops had pushed 38 miles into Tigray; Eritrea called that a 'declaration of war', and Ethiopian drones reportedly struck Eritrean forces near Adigrat. Lead with the two letters. The mechanism: Abiy's stated aim of regaining the port of Assab, an Egypt–Eritrea–Somalia–Sudan bloc pledged to coordinate militarily, and Ethiopia's imports running on a single highway to Djibouti that rebels have already threatened. Report only the documented facts (UN letters, AFP and Reuters figures), not the outlet's analysis.

stories.label: Trump's 'Shield of the Americas' is more fragile than it seems
stories.summary: Costa Rica opens a 5,100-inmate maximum-security prison today, built for $35 million on the model of Bukele's CECOT. Lead with that, then the LAPOP AmericasBarometer data: in 8 of 11 Shield of the Americas countries more voters back the opposition than the president, and trust in the US government has fallen to 45% (from 87% to 40% in Panama). The mechanism: unpopular governments entrench emergency powers and mega-prisons, funded by Washington ($52m in redirected military financing, $1bn for Colombia), which successors will inherit — Ecuador's curfew arrested 5,023, of whom 14% had organised-crime ties. Dateline San José.

stories.label: IN BRIEF: First hearing of Nord Stream blast case takes place in Germany
stories.summary: The first trial over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage opened at Hamburg's Higher Regional Court, with Ukrainian national Serhii Kuznietsov as defendant, four years after the blasts. Lead with the precedent: a German court trying a citizen of an ally for destroying critical infrastructure Germany co-owned. State-media-only source: attribute to Russian state news agency TASS throughout.

stories.label: In Gaza, even cash comes at a cost
stories.summary: Israel's restrictions on banknote transfers into Gaza have run the territory's cash supply down, so Palestinians pay commissions just to withdraw their own money. Lead with the commission rate the reporting gives. The mechanism: control of the physical currency is a siege instrument that taxes every purchase, with Israel holding the levers over Gaza's shekel supply.

stories.label: BYD expands EV shipping fleet as wars upend freight costs and key trade routes
stories.summary: China's largest EV maker is buying its own car-carrier ships because a shortage of vessels and war-driven freight costs are holding back its exports. Lead with the fleet size and the freight cost. The mechanism: with Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disrupted, carmakers are vertically integrating shipping. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.

stories.label: Data centre of Russia's largest bank hit by drone
stories.summary: A drone hit a Sberbank data centre in Balakovo, Saratov region, a Sberbank executive said; services kept running. Lead with the target: the latest in a Ukrainian campaign against Russian internet and data infrastructure, which has reached Yandex too. The mechanism: the war has moved from refineries to the servers that run a state bank, during a period when Kyiv has paused refinery strikes for the energy truce. Dateline Balakovo.

stories.label: Microsoft takes down 3 major phishing platforms used by Chinese cybercriminals
stories.summary: Microsoft, Japan's National Police Agency and the hospital-security group Health-ISAC got a US court order to seize the domains behind YAM Store, CoGUI and Iron Man, phishing-as-a-service kits sold to criminals. Lead with the mechanism: a private company uses a civil court order to dismantle criminal infrastructure across borders, a role usually held by police. Name the victims the kits targeted.

stories.label: The Internet's undersea backbone is slipping into the danger zone
stories.summary: Most of the world's internet traffic still runs through subsea cables, and wars from Hormuz to the Baltic are putting them inside conflict zones where UNCLOS gives little protection. Lead with the figure for traffic or cable faults the piece reports. The mechanism: cables share the seabed with pipelines and power lines, and repair ships cannot reach war zones. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Reflect Orbital Buys Two Skyroot Aerospace Launches
stories.summary: Reflect Orbital, the US startup that wants to beam sunlight to the ground from orbiting mirrors, has bought two launches from India's private Skyroot Aerospace. Lead with what the mirrors would do to the night sky, a concern astronomers have raised. The mechanism: an Indian private launcher winning US customers as Western launch capacity runs short. Dateline Hyderabad.

stories.label: Jamming the flow to enable memory in quantum materials
stories.summary: Researchers showed that jamming the structural flow during a coupled structural–electronic phase transition gives a material built-in memory of its past state, the behaviour neuromorphic chips need to mimic synapses. Lead with what the material remembers and how. Name the journal and the lab; explain why brain-like hardware needs it.

stories.label: Ukraine Says New Starlink Speed Limit Is Disrupting Its Attacks
stories.summary: SpaceX throttled Starlink terminals in Ukraine overnight with no warning, and a presidential adviser says military missions were disrupted. Lead with the dependency: one private company's switch decides whether a state's drone and strike operations run. The mechanism to explain is how a speed cap degrades drone control links, and who in the US decides it.

stories.label: IMF chief calls for 'urgent repairs' to address fiscal balances
stories.summary: New since the IMF's debt warning: in Bangkok on Oct 14 Georgieva said the attacks on Saudi Arabia could spill over into every economy, and told governments that resilience has reached its limits. Lead with the Saudi spillover and who pays it — oil importers in Asia and Africa already squeezed by debt service — then the fiscal repair she demands. Name Brent crude and the US 10-year Treasury yield as the channels.

stories.label: Anti-drug crusader's murder: Mob sets ablaze accused's medical store in Mansa amid bulldozer action
stories.summary: Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead in daylight while streaming on Facebook; the next day Punjab authorities demolished part of the accused pharmacist's house and a mob burned his shop. Two failures to lead with: a state where activists who expose drug sales get killed, and a state that answers with bulldozer punishment before any trial. NDTV frames the wider pattern of activist killings in Punjab.

stories.label: China's exports surge amid AI-driven demand
stories.summary: China's September exports jumped 36.3% year on year to $447.18bn, up from 25% in August. Lead with the number and what drives it — AI hardware demand — then who absorbs the surplus: the EU, Southeast Asia and Global South markets as US tariffs divert flows. Name the yuan.

stories.label: Turkish police raid office of opposition TV channel, the broadcaster says
stories.summary: Hundreds of police entered Halk TV's Istanbul building and its live broadcast was cut at 06:30, replaced by pre-recorded material. Lead with the cut feed: an opposition channel taken off air by a search. Explain the trustee mechanism Ankara has used to seize opposition media and companies, and what it leaves of Turkey's independent broadcasting.

stories.label: No meio do caminho tinha uma norma – o que explica mortes causadas por policiais da Bahia
stories.summary: Agência Pública traces Bahia's police killings — the highest of any Brazilian state — to a 2019 normative instruction that made it harder to investigate military police. Lead with the rule and its effect on accountability: who signed it, how it shields officers, and who dies, overwhelmingly young Black men in Salvador's periphery.

stories.label: Nvidia’s China AI-chip share falls to 34% as Huawei reaches 28%
stories.summary: An IDC report puts Nvidia at 34% of China's data-centre AI accelerator market in the first half of 2026, with Huawei at 28%; Nvidia's China shipments fell 44% to 678,000. Lead with the gap closing: US export controls built the market for China's own chips. The mechanism is supply restriction turning into import substitution.

stories.label: OpenAI拟收购Trail of Bits，加码网络安全业务
stories.summary: OpenAI is in early talks to buy Trail of Bits, the open-source security firm that took second in DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge and ran the 'Patch the Planet' programme with OpenAI's tools in June (per The Information, via Zhidx). Lead with what moves inside a model maker: one of the independent auditors open-source software relies on. The tension: AI labs both build bug-finding models and restrict them for the public.

stories.label: Coinbase, which holds 5% of all bitcoin, wants the quantum fix started now
stories.summary: Coinbase, custodian of about 5% of all bitcoin, wants the network to begin its migration to quantum-resistant signatures now and to split off the fight over dormant wallets so it does not stall the fix. Lead with the exposure: which coins have public keys already visible, and the governance problem of a network with no one to order an upgrade. Name bitcoin.

stories.label: Evidence for maternal autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of preterm birth - Nature Immunology
stories.summary: A Nature Immunology study finds that mothers who deliver preterm share an autoantibody signature that term pregnancies lack, against a control group of 204. Lead with the finding: some preterm births may be the mother's immune system attacking, which points to a blood test and to treatments. Preterm birth is the leading killer of young children, most of them in South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa.

stories.label: Global deforestation slowed in 2025 but surged in Congo basin: Study
stories.summary: A new study finds global deforestation slowed in 2025 while forest loss surged in the Congo basin, and warns a strong El Niño will undo the gains. Lead with the divergence: the world's second-largest rainforest is now where the loss concentrates. Explain what drives it in DR Congo and Cameroon, and who lives off that forest.

stories.label: Aramco building targeted after Saudi-led coalition hits Houthi site | The National
stories.summary: A missile set fire to a Saudi Aramco administrative building in Dhahran overnight, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said, after a Saudi-led coalition strike on a Houthi site in Sanaa. The war has now reached the Eastern Province, home of the kingdom's oil industry, not only Riyadh's airport. Lead with the target, then the mechanism: Trump accused the Houthis of trying to push up oil prices 'at Iran's behest' before the US elections, and the reader should see what a strike near Aramco's headquarters does to Brent crude and to the war-risk premium on Gulf cargoes. Name the Yemeni civilians under the coalition strikes on Sanaa with the same weight as the Saudi side.

stories.label: Japan urges Russia for 'impartial treatment' of arrested journalist
stories.summary: Russia's FSB has charged Yuki Imai, a Hokkaido Shimbun reporter, with espionage after detaining him on Sakhalin, accusing him of gathering information on Moscow's defence capabilities for Tokyo. Lead with the charge and what it carries; the mechanism is a pattern: Russia has used espionage charges against foreign reporters (Evan Gershkovich) as leverage, and Japan, which sanctions Russia and arms Ukraine indirectly, has little to trade. Note Tokyo's muted wording, 'impartial treatment', against what it would say if an ally held its reporter.

stories.label: Trump's ambassador to Greece asked to resign amid misconduct allegations
stories.summary: Trump asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, US ambassador to Greece, to resign after reports that she sought $100,000 from a Trump supporter to pay personal credit-card debt and took luxury trips and hotel stays from wealthy Greek businessmen; she denies wrongdoing and has vowed to fight. Lead with the specific gifts and who gave them: the accountability question is what Greek business interests sought from the US embassy in Athens, a key post for East Med energy and arms deals. Dateline Athens.

stories.label: DR Congo Ebola cases pass 9,000 as efforts to curb transmission falter
stories.summary: The Health Ministry reports 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, a fatality rate near half, up from the 4,000 deaths reported on 2 October. Lead with the new count and the twelve-day rise. The mechanism: transmission is outrunning vaccination and contact tracing in Ituri and the east, where M23's advance and Kabila's new alliance with it fracture the state that would run the response. Name who funds the response and what has been cut.

stories.label: US fines Bank of America $1.2bn for money laundering, sanctions violations
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed more than $1.21bn in penalties on Bank of America, the second-largest US bank, for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, including the third-largest penalty in the department's history. Lead with the size and with what the bank let through: which sanctioned parties and jurisdictions, over how many years, and how much money moved. The structural point: the same Treasury that enforces sanctions on others found its second-biggest bank processing the flows, and a fine is a fraction of a quarter's profit.

stories.label: Why the IMF is worried about a global debt squeeze as bond yields climb
stories.summary: New since yesterday's growth forecast: the IMF's fiscal warning that rising borrowing costs, with the US 10-year Treasury yield at a 24-year high, are straining public finances worldwide. Lead with the transmission: when US yields rise, emerging and Muslim-majority borrowers (Pakistan, Egypt, Nigeria) refinance dearer and cut spending on their own people to pay creditors. Give the IMF's numbers on debt-service share of revenue where the report has them, and name the series: the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: Shell to sell Nigeria's domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy
stories.summary: Shell has agreed to sell all of Shell Nigeria Gas, which pipes gas to factories and power users at home, to Vaaris Energy. Lead with what changes hands and the price if disclosed; the mechanism is the long Western exit from Nigerian onshore assets (Shell's 2025 onshore sale to Renaissance, Exxon, Eni) while the majors keep the deepwater and export LNG. Who inherits the pipelines, the liabilities and the Niger Delta communities, and whether domestic supply gets cheaper or less reliable.

stories.label: OpenAI employee arrested for planting recording device at office
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national working as an OpenAI engineer, and charged him over a recording device found behind a television in an OpenAI conference room in San Francisco. Lead with what was found and the charge, stated as allegations. The structural point: frontier labs are now treated as national-security targets, and the reader should know what the complaint says about motive or any foreign link, and what it does not; do not imply state direction the charging papers do not allege.

stories.label: Claude写代码太快，Anthropic先扛不住了：连Git都要重做
stories.summary: Anthropic has replaced Git in its monorepo with Scion, a server-side source-control system built by seven people in five months, because AI agents now merge over 30,000 changes a day, up twelvefold from about 2,500 in May. Lead with the load: about 25 million CI checkouts a day and an estimated 600PB of Git traffic, a main-branch history near 100GB. The mechanism for developers: always-online clients, server-side commits and merges, changesets in a write-ahead log on Spanner, virtualised sparse checkouts, a footprint 1/200 of the Git mirrors. The point: tools built for human-paced coding break first when agents write the code. Anthropic says it will not release Scion as a product.

stories.label: Gemini 4 Argon全球上线，API限时五折，谷歌要杀回第一梯队！
stories.summary: Google has opened Gemini 4 Argon, its flagship model announced 1 October, to developers and businesses worldwide at a launch price cut by half: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, with cached input 95% off, until 30 November. Lead with the price: it is a bid to win agent workloads back from OpenAI and Anthropic, and the reader should see how it compares per token. Report the benchmark claims (first on the Vals Index) as Google's own, and the demos (CAD from a sketch, 1,000 self-checking iterations) as demos.

stories.label: Isle of Wight fossil sheds light on enigmatic meat-eating dinosaurs
stories.summary: Researchers have named Invictibellatrix amberina, an early megaraptoran found on the Isle of Wight, the first of this Cretaceous lineage of carnivores known from Europe; until now they were known mostly from South America, Australia and Asia. Lead with where it was found and why that is surprising; the mechanism is biogeography: an early European member bears on where megaraptorans arose and how they spread before the continents parted. Name the journal and the skull features the paper adds.

stories.label: PTI protest in Bara turns violent as demonstrators clash with police
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the arrests of PTI workers and legislators in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (one clause): the crackdown has met resistance on the street. A PTI protest in Bara tehsil, Khyber district, turned violent on Tuesday; Dawn reports police firing live rounds and tear gas, protesters manhandling officers, and government buildings set on fire. Lead with the live fire and the burned buildings, and any casualties the page confirms (it cites Hayatabad Medical Complex). Mechanism: say what the protest was called against, who ordered the police response, and why Bara, an Afridi tribal area merged into the province only in 2018, is where a party dispute turns into a confrontation with the state. Say what Dawn could verify and what it could not, and give the provincial and federal governments' and PTI's accounts as their own. Single source, the Pakistani paper of record. Write your own headline. Dateline Bara.

stories.label: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
stories.summary: Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution renewed for 15 days the detention of six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsda2sh (Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal) in Case 8083/2026, their lawyers say. Lead with six fact-checkers held and the renewal. Mechanism: pretrial detention in Egypt is renewed in 15-day blocks by the same prosecution that brings the case, so a person can be held for months or years without trial; say what the six are accused of, when they were arrested, and what the platform published. Set it beside the draft law reported this afternoon that would ban jailing journalists in publishing cases (one clause): the constitution already forbids it, and this is the practice the bill is aimed at. Give the prosecution's position, or that it has given none. Mada Masr is the Egyptian outlet and is itself blocked in Egypt. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Destruction of Gaza Court System Strips Women of Their Rights
stories.summary: With Gaza's courts destroyed, Palestinian women cannot enforce rights to inheritance, divorce, alimony and property, Drop Site reports. Lead with the women the report names and what each cannot obtain. Mechanism: family law in Gaza runs through sharia courts whose buildings, archives and judges the war destroyed or scattered, so a widow cannot prove a marriage or a death, register an inheritance or collect maintenance; say how many courts functioned before and how many do now, what happened to the records, and what stand-ins (informal committees, clan mediation) decide in their place and in whose favour. The accountability point: the destruction of a judiciary has a named author, and its cost falls on those with the least power inside the society; give the Israeli authorities' and Gaza authorities' replies if the page has them. Distinct from this morning's piece on families sleeping in damaged buildings; do not retell it. Drop Site uses the word genocide; attribute characterisations and write the facts. No regional outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Gaza City, or as the report places it.

stories.label: Trump says he does not believe China and Russia help Iran, contradicting US intelligence
stories.summary: President Trump said on Truth Social that he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran 'at all', while US intelligence reports in recent months have found that both directly support Tehran. Lead with the contradiction: the commander of a war publicly rejecting his own agencies' finding about who is supplying the other side. Mechanism: say what the intelligence reports found (what kind of support, as the pages give it), what prompted the post, and what follows from the president's position: no sanctions or pressure on Beijing and Moscow over Iran, at a moment when the US is enforcing a blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and negotiating with both powers on other files. Give Beijing's, Moscow's and Tehran's statements if a page has them. One clause on today's Hormuz attacks at most; do not retell them. Write from Al-Monitor (a Reuters report); the Middle East Eye link is a live-blog entry carrying the same text. State the intelligence findings as reported, not as established. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: UK ambassador summoned to Iran's foreign ministry
stories.summary: New since Monday's piece on London blaming Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the incident at RAF Fairford, the airbase used by US forces (one clause): Tehran has answered formally. Iran's foreign ministry summoned the British ambassador, Hugo Shorter, on Tuesday to protest what it calls baseless allegations, the Iranian state news agency Mehr reports; assistant foreign minister Alireza Yousefi delivered the protest. Lead with the summons and what Iran told the ambassador. Mechanism: say what Britain alleged and on what published evidence, what Iran denies, and what each side can do next (expulsions, proscription of the Guards, which London has long debated), with Britain hosting US aircraft used in the war on Iran. Mehr is Iranian state media and the only source: attribute every claim to it and to the ministry, state nothing as fact beyond the summons itself, and do not carry Tehran's adjectives. No independent or British outlet in the feed carries it. Write your own headline. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: After flood disasters, Nepal needs clear numbers on aid and a reconstruction plan
stories.summary: Nepal's flood-hit communities are waiting on rebuilding while nobody can say how much aid has arrived or where it went, Global Voices reports. Lead with the people still without homes and the missing figures, not the floods themselves. Mechanism: say what was destroyed (homes, roads, bridges, livelihoods, with the counts the page gives), how much relief was pledged and by whom, which body is responsible for accounting for it, and why there is no reconstruction plan: who decides between federal, provincial and local government. The accountability point: after a disaster the money is the story, and Nepal's 2015 earthquake reconstruction is the precedent readers should be given in a clause if the page gives it. This is a politics story about aid and the state, not a weather or science story. The headline is the outlet's argument: write the reported facts, attribute judgments to the people quoted, and write your own neutral headline. Single source. Dateline as the report places it (Kathmandu or the affected district).

stories.label: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.03
stories.summary: Pakistan cut petrol by Rs2.71 to Rs392.66 a litre and diesel by three paisa to Rs396.82, while the state keeps taking Rs114 on every litre in taxes and levies. Lead with the tax, not the cut: more than a quarter of what a Pakistani pays at the pump is the government's share, and the fortnightly revision moved the price by under 1%. Mechanism: say how the price is built (import cost tracking the price of Brent crude and the rupee, then the petroleum levy, climate levy and margins, as the page breaks them down), why the levy is where it is (IMF programme revenue targets), and why diesel, the fuel of freight and farm tractors, barely moved. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, with the Strait of Hormuz closure behind it. Who it lands on: households and transporters in a country the UNDP index reported this morning (one clause) as poorer than its neighbours. Give the minister's statement as the page has it. Single source, Dawn. Write your own headline. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Parks Tau brought the transformation fight to the automotive industry
stories.summary: South Africa's trade minister, Parks Tau, used a keynote to the motor industry to demand more Black ownership and more locally made parts from the foreign carmakers that assemble there. Lead with what he asked for and of whom: the targets, the deadline and the incentives at stake, as the page gives them. Mechanism: the plants belong to Toyota, VW, BMW, Mercedes, Ford and others and exist because of a state incentive scheme, so the government's lever is the subsidy; the carmakers' lever is that they can leave, with US tariffs, cheap Chinese imports and the shift to plug-in vehicles already squeezing exports. Say how much local content the industry has against its target and what the manufacturers answered. Who it lands on: more than 100,000 autoworkers and the Black-owned suppliers the policy is meant to create. The page is labelled analysis: write the announcements and figures as news and attribute judgments to Daily Maverick. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the speech.

stories.label: 一只18A“超购王”的停摆：停牌半年、调出港股通，中慧生物年内第三位董事辞任
stories.summary: A Chinese biotech that was among the most oversubscribed listings under Hong Kong's Chapter 18A, the rule that lets drug developers with no revenue go public, has been suspended from trading for half a year, removed from the Stock Connect scheme that lets mainland investors buy it, and has just lost its third director this year, TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports. Lead with the retail investors locked in: the shares cannot be sold, the annual report has not been filed, and an independent forensic investigation is under way. Mechanism: say what 18A allows and why it drew a rush of subscriptions, what triggered the suspension (the auditor, the unfiled accounts, what the forensic inquiry is examining), what removal from Stock Connect does to mainland holders, and what the exchange's delisting clock is. The structural point: Hong Kong reopened its IPO market on pre-revenue biotech, and this is what a failure in that regime looks like. In Chinese; translate the company name (Zhonghui Biotech, 中慧生物), figures and dates exactly, attribute to TMTPost, state allegations as allegations. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Hong Kong.

stories.label: Walmart to offer 250-plus free medications, including GLP-1s, to employees
stories.summary: Walmart, the largest private employer in the United States, will give employees more than 250 medications at no cost, including GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs, insulin and inhalers. Lead with the scale: how many workers are covered and from when, and that the list includes drugs that cost hundreds of dollars a month. Mechanism: Walmart insures its own workforce and runs its own pharmacies, so it buys the drugs at its own cost and pays its own claims; say who qualifies (which health plans, full-time or part-time), what the company expects to save or spend, and what it means for the drugmakers and for other employers that have been dropping GLP-1 coverage as too expensive. Who it lands on: low-wage workers in a country where a job decides whether insulin is affordable. Walmart's shares are up 7.6% in a week: say so only if the page ties the move to a cause, and do not attribute it to this plan yourself. Reuters brief, single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Bentonville. US dateline (4 of 3: see summary).

stories.label: Can GLP-1s heal the brain? Obesity drugs get a makeover for addiction and depression
stories.summary: Drug companies are now developing GLP-1-related compounds, the class behind the obesity drugs, to treat addiction, schizophrenia, depression and other brain disorders, building on years of academic work, Nature reports. Lead with the shift: a gut-hormone drug being re-engineered for the brain, with new money behind it. Mechanism for a technical reader: say where GLP-1 receptors sit in the brain and what they do to reward and craving, what the evidence is so far and of what kind (observational data from people taking the drugs for weight, animal studies, which randomised trials have reported and what they found), why existing drugs reach the brain poorly and how the new compounds differ, and which companies and trials the piece names. Say what is not shown: the trials that failed or were null, and the psychiatric side-effect questions. This is Nature's news reporting, not a paper: attribute to Nature and the researchers it quotes, and state no effect as established that the trials have not established. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places it.

stories.label: Character.ai's Bankruptcy Documents Show the Economics of AI Don't Work
stories.summary: Character.ai's bankruptcy filings show a consumer AI company that degraded its product to cut costs and raise revenue and was still burning cash, 404 Media reports. Lead with the numbers in the court documents: revenue, what it cost to run the models, the losses, the debts and to whom. Mechanism for a technical reader: every message a user sends costs compute, so usage that would be profit for a normal app is cost here; say what the company did to close the gap (ads, paywalls, cheaper models, limits) and why the filings say it was not enough, who the creditors are (cloud providers, investors), and what happens to users' conversations and to the lawsuits over harm to minors in a bankruptcy. The structural point: one of the most-used chatbot products could not cover inference with subscriptions, which is a data point about the whole sector. The feed entry is a one-line teaser: read the page first and write only what the filings, as 404 Media reports them, support; the headline's generalisation is the outlet's. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the filing's court. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: ESA targets Anbernic emulation handhelds as "superfake" piracy enablers
stories.summary: The Entertainment Software Association, the US video-game industry's trade group (the feed's tags confuse it with the European Space Agency; it is not), has asked the US Trade Representative to act against Anbernic, a Chinese maker of handheld Android consoles built for retro emulation. Lead with the request and its target: a hardware maker, not a site hosting pirated games. Mechanism for a technical reader: say what the ESA asked for (listing on the USTR's notorious-markets review, as the page gives it) and what that listing does and does not do legally, what 'superfake' means in the filing, and where the legal line sits: emulators are lawful in the US, pre-loaded copyrighted ROMs are not, and the filing argues the devices ship with or steer buyers to the latter. Say what Anbernic sells and answers. The structural point: a trade lobby using trade policy against a foreign device maker where copyright suits have not reached, with implications for every open handheld. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: 在AI时代“改变世界”，买电、买算力，还是造底座？
stories.summary: Envision, the Chinese wind-turbine and battery group, says it has built at Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia what it calls the world's largest single AI computing block: a 120,000-square-metre data centre fed more than 80% by its own wind farms over a dedicated line, and it plans 5 GW of such desert sites by 2030 under a programme named Mission Gobi, Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports. Lead with the design choice: put the computing where the wind and sun are, and plan generation, storage and servers as one system off the public grid. Mechanism for a technical reader: say why that is hard (intermittent supply against a load that runs around the clock, with no grid behind it), and what Envision says it uses: forecasting and dispatch models, battery storage, an 800-volt direct-current feed through solid-state transformers that removes conversion steps, liquid cooling, and domestic chips. The structural point is the view from inside China's industry: the binding constraint on AI has moved from chips to electricity, substations take 12 to 18 months and customers want capacity in six, and a turbine maker is entering the data-centre business from the power side. The piece is admiring and reads close to company material: state every figure and every superlative as Envision's claim, leave out the Fortune list, and say what is not independently shown (how the site runs when the wind drops, actual utilisation, cost per unit of compute). In Chinese; translate names and specifications exactly. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Ulanqab.
